hook.line: Bogotá is cold, the day is long and Tomás has not eaten. Spanish speakers exaggerate how they feel all the time, and they mostly do it by dying.

examples.es: Me moría de sueño en esa reunión.
examples.en: I was dead tired in that meeting.

examples.es: Me muero de ganas de verte.
examples.en: I'm dying to see you. (to a friend)

examples.es: Tomás se muere de frío en Bogotá.
examples.en: Tomás is freezing to death in Bogotá.

examples.es: Mariana se murió de la vergüenza cuando Simón habló.
examples.en: Mariana died of embarrassment when Simón spoke.

rule:
*Morirse de* plus a feeling means "dying of", and it just says "very much": *hambre*, *frío*, *calor*, *sueño*, *miedo*, *vergüenza*.
It is reflexive, so the small word changes with the person: *me muero*, *te mueres*, *se muere*, *nos morimos*.
With *risa* and *vergüenza* people often add *la*: *de la risa*.
For "dying to do something", use *de ganas de* plus the infinitive: *Me muero de ganas de verte.*
Nobody is in danger. It is exaggeration.
smallPrint: Teachers call this hyperbole: a deliberate exaggeration that nobody takes literally.

readAndPick.es: Tomás se muere de frío en Bogotá.
options: Tomás is dying of heat in Bogotá.
Are you dead tired? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Me muero de ganas de verte.
options: I'm dying to see you. (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Se morían de la risa con Simón.
options: They were dying of fear because of Simón.
They were dying of laughter at Simón.

readAndPick.es: Mis amigos se mueren de calor en Cartagena.
options: My friends are sweltering in Cartagena.
My friends are freezing in Cartagena.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de* or *por*, then type the whole sentence: Me muero ___ hambre. (I'm starving.)
Choose *me* or *se*, then type the whole sentence: Tomás ___ muere de frío en Bogotá. (Tomás is freezing to death in Bogotá.)
yourTurn.answer: Tomás se muere de frío en Bogotá.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm dying of heat.
Type it in Spanish: We nearly died laughing.
Type it in Spanish: I'm dying to see you. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Me muero de ganas de verte.
yourTurn.why: *Ganas de* plus an infinitive is "dying to".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about you all: *Me muero de frío.* becomes: You all are freezing. (to a group)
Make it a question to a friend: *Tienes hambre.* becomes: Are you starving? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Te mueres de* asks it in exaggerated form.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish says it with the small word: *me muero*, or *me estoy muriendo*.
Almost. The feeling you die of comes after *de*, not *por*.

pitfalls.right: Me muero de ganas de verte.
pitfalls.why: Almost. "Dying to" needs *ganas*: *de ganas de* plus an infinitive.

personal: Tell me what you're dying of right now. Use *me muero de…*.
